AMD Has Ripped 170% This Year: Is It Too Late to Buy? ©@Alexander's Images via Canva, @Nicolas Foster from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

AMD stock is up 170% in 2026, carried by two record data center quarters and Meta's deal for up to 6 gigawatts of its AI chips.

Intel ran nearly as far on demand for server chips, while Nvidia lagged and trades at less than half AMD's forward multiple.

October's AI-financing scare cut AMD's multiple while analysts kept expecting its normalized EPS to more than double in 2027.

The Nov. 3 report is the first test of that doubling, and if it holds, AMD isn't too late to buy.

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) stock is up 170% in 2026, and the business earned most of it: two record data center quarters and a deal with Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) for up to 6 gigawatts of its Instinct GPUs.

The chip rally helped too. Intel (INTC:NASDAQ) is up 159% this year on the same hunger for server chips, while Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) has gained just 15% and trades at well under half AMD's forward multiple. So what does AMD's premium pay for?

From a February stumble to two record quarters

The year started badly. On Feb. 3, AMD guided first-quarter revenue below the quarter it had just reported, and the stock lost 17% the next day.

Three weeks later, Meta signed on for up to 6 gigawatts of Instinct GPUs with a warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares.

Then the numbers showed up. First-quarter revenue came in at $10.25 billion, against the $9.89 billion analysts expected, with data center sales up 57%. In the second quarter, revenue rose 50% to $11.5 billion, data center sales more than doubled to $6.7 billion, and AMD guided to about $13 billion for the third quarter.

Intel's run rests on part of the same story. AMD raised its forecast for the 2030 server CPU market to about $220 billion, from about $60 billion, in nine months, as AI agents eat up CPUs. New Street Research upgraded Intel to Buy on Oct. 26, arguing that server CPU supply will stay tight for years, so Intel's third-quarter report, due before AMD's, is a read on AMD's server business.

TIKR tracks 55 analysts on AMD. How many say "Buy"?

October took some of the froth off

AMD closed at a record on Oct. 6, the day CEO Lisa Su said it would raise supply substantially in 2027. Then fears over who pays for AI data centers hit chip stocks, and AMD now sits [12%] below that high.

Analysts didn't cut their numbers through the drop. They still see normalized EPS more than doubling, from $7.61 this year to $15.85 in 2027:

title: Walmart, Eli Lilly and Cigna File Objections to ICE and OKX’s Tokenized Stock Venue

Walmart, Eli Lilly and Cigna File Objections to ICE and OKX’s Tokenized Stock Venue

Walmart, Eli Lilly, Cigna, Carnival and Arcos Dorados have joined the companies objecting to tokenized trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, the venue that Intercontinental Exchange and OKX own together.

A public notice from the venue dated Oct. 28 lists 38 issuers under its "Notice of Issuer Objection" heading. The five companies above are the only names on it that did not appear in the Oct. 27 version, which counted 33 objectors, including JPMorgan, AMD and Coca-Cola.

As in earlier versions, the notice does not explain why any company objected. It also gives no date for when trading will start.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter.

A List That Keeps Growing

Under the SEC exemption that allows onchain trading of tokenized stocks, a company that files a timely written objection keeps a third-party token of its stock off the venue, and the venue has to disclose the objection in an updated notice.

The Oct. 8 notice already listed four objectors, and every update since has added names. The count reached nine on Oct. 15, 16 on Oct. 19, 22 on Oct. 23 and 26 on Oct. 26 before hitting 33 on Oct. 27. Earlier objectors include Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Broadcom and UnitedHealth.

How the Venue Would Work

OKXICE LLC, the Texas company behind the venue, is split 50/50 between ICE and OKC USA Holding Inc., an OKX affiliate. Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on X Layer, the Ethereum layer-2 network OKX launched, with access limited to wallets holding a soulbound token the venue issues. The notice says it will operate 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

The risk section is unchanged on governance. Upgrades to the venue's smart contracts need sign-off from several authorized staff. Even so, changes "take effect without a timelock, so TSV Participants may receive no advance notice of an upgrade," the notice says.

ICE and OKX formed the joint venture to bring tokenized equities to market, with former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo as co-chair.

Marvell Technology (MRVL) stock returned 184.2% over the past year, against 14.0% for the S&P 500. Following a gain of that size, you want to know what could still surprise investors. That is difficult to judge at Marvell. Management already counts its newest custom chip deal in its sales outlook through fiscal 2028, and says the bigger payoff comes later. So what is that deal, and how far along is it?

Marvell Expanded A Custom Chip Deal With A Hyperscaler

Marvell disclosed an expanded commercial agreement, which includes a warrant, with a key hyperscaler during the week before its August 27, 2026 call. Management described the customer as one of the largest adopters of custom silicon, adding that the warrant reflects the scale and long-term potential of the relationship. The chips include parts that attach to the TPU ecosystem, such as AI inference accelerators, storage controllers and network interface controllers.

Custom work spans years, and the agreement reflects that timeline. It covers programs awarded to Marvell over the past several years that are currently in execution, along with new design wins and future potential programs. Management said the revenue these programs bring through fiscal 2028 is already in its custom revenue target. The big impact, management noted, would arrive in fiscal 2029 and beyond. This later period represents the opportunity still ahead of the reported numbers.

Early evidence indicates the custom business is selling today. Management named custom, alongside interconnect and switching, among the data center businesses seeing strong tailwinds in fiscal Q2 2027. The company expects custom to ramp significantly in the second half of fiscal 2027.

How Fast Could Marvell's Custom Business Grow?

Management expects custom to more than double in fiscal 2028. Custom belongs to the data center business, which accounted for 79% of Marvell's revenue in fiscal Q2 2027. On the August call, however, management named interconnect rather than custom as the business leading Marvell's growth.

During the August call, management raised its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook by $1.5 billion from the projection provided a quarter earlier. Executives said some of that raise comes from custom without putting a number on it. News reports indicated Marvell established a revenue target of $70 billion to $90 billion for fiscal 2031 at its October 6, 2026 Investor Day. That target covers all of Marvell rather than custom alone. The same reports said Marvell also lifted its fiscal 2028 sales outlook at that event, to about $20 billion.
